title: Sentiment
subtitle: How professional investors on X reacted to the latest earnings, ranked by reach, with the analysts' views alongside.

body: Across the hyperscalers, the market rewarded whoever funds AI from its own cash and punished cash burn, even with fast cloud growth. Microsoft is the only one still cash positive. Alphabet, Meta and Amazon all reported negative free cash flow and all sold off.

The professional accounts with the most reach (The Transcript, Fiscal.ai, Beth Kindig, Bespoke, Wall St Engine) all framed the season around free cash flow and capex, not revenue beats. Meta's record CDS spreads show the debate has spread to credit.

tickers.topTheme: AI Mode earns less per search, FCF -$9.1B

facts.label: Earnings
facts.value: Oct 28, after the close

facts.label: Stock reaction
facts.value: Down about 12% to 13% on Oct 29, worst post-earnings day on record per CNBC, roughly $500B of value lost

facts.label: Sentiment
facts.value: Bearish near term, pros still constructive on 12 months

facts.label: Street moves
facts.value: Citizens downgraded to market perform. BofA cut target to $380, BMO to $425, UBS to $332. Morgan Stanley held $375

tickers.before: Pros wanted Search and YouTube ad growth to hold while Cloud grew about 90% and capex stayed at $195B to $205B. Beth Kindig flagged Alphabet as expected to burn cash for a second straight quarter.
tickers.after: First top and bottom line miss in nearly four years. Cloud grew 103% to $30.7B, but Search was $63.35B against about $64.9B expected and free cash flow was negative $9.07B. The narrative that stuck: Philipp Schindler said AI Mode queries had an impact because of lower monetization in AI Mode. Pros framed it as more searches but less money per search, plus a cash burn problem, while Microsoft showed you can grow AI and stay cash positive.
tickers.controversy: The ad gouging story is mostly anecdotal. Advertiser complaints about rising cost per click got replies but little reach. The 10-Q data cited by several analysts shows paid clicks up 8% (down from 13% in the first half) and cost per click up only 4%. So the miss was fewer monetized clicks, not price hikes. Rahul Sharma, a former Citi and Alliance Capital fund manager, made this point. The real controversy for advertisers is that AI Mode answers carry fewer ads, and Google says it will add more ads inside AI Mode, including outside the US.

tickers.before: Kindig noted Microsoft was the only hyperscaler expected to stay cash positive. Visible Alpha had Azure at about 47.7%.
tickers.after: Azure grew 48% to $33.2B, and Microsoft gave a dollar figure for it for the first time. It guided 49% to 50% next quarter against about 44.6% expected. Revenue was $92.3B against $90.7B expected. Capex of $45.2B came in under estimates, and calendar 2026 capex was trimmed to about $170B because third-party capacity came late. Free cash flow fell 27% but stayed positive at $18.6B. Pros' read: it is the self-funding AI winner. The one worry is that lower capex reflects timing, not discipline.

tickers.topTheme: AWS fastest in 5 years vs -$42B trailing FCF

facts.label: Earnings
facts.value: Oct 29, after the close

facts.label: Stock reaction
facts.value: Closed Oct 29 at $243.79 (down 4.25% before the print), then down about 7% premarket Oct 30 near $226 to $227

facts.label: Sentiment
facts.value: Mixed, leaning bearish on cash

tickers.before: Morgan Stanley's model, shared by Kindig, has AWS growing about 47% in 2027. Pros expected AWS at about 38% and a third straight quarter of cash burn.
tickers.after: AWS grew 39.3% to $46.0B, its fastest in nearly five years, and the backlog is $578B. Jassy guided AWS to over 40% growth in both 2027 and 2028. But revenue of $201.9B and EPS of $1.89 missed, the Q4 guide midpoints were below consensus, capex was $77.3B in a single quarter, and trailing free cash flow was negative $42.4B. The operating margin hit a record 13.9%. The pros' split: AWS is accelerating, but the stock is priced on the cash bill.

tickers.topTheme: First negative FCF since 2012, record CDS, Class C shares

facts.label: Earnings
facts.value: Oct 21, after the close

facts.label: Stock reaction
facts.value: Up about 2.5% to 4% after hours, then down nearly 7% on Oct 22 (about $651)

facts.label: Sentiment
facts.value: Mixed: Street bullish, tape and credit market bearish

facts.label: Street moves
facts.value: 6 of 7 firms raised targets per Benzinga. Susquehanna to $850. JPMorgan cut to $800

tickers.before: Baird's ad checks were positive and it expected an in-line quarter. The question was whether a capex raise would be forgiven now that AI is improving ad returns.
tickers.after: Revenue was $64.6B, up 26%, ahead of $63.4B expected, and the Q4 guide was strong at $73B to $76B. EPS of $3.83 included a $9.9B legal charge for the social media harm settlements. Capex of $34.9B pushed free cash flow to negative $2.12B, the first negative quarter since 2012. Meta also created a nonvoting Class C stock, which the market read as a way to raise equity without diluting votes, and its 5-year CDS hit a record. The debate moved from the stock to the credit market.
tickers.controversy: The nonvoting Class C share plus record CDS spreads is the issue professionals focused on: is Meta preparing to fund AI with new equity?

facts.label: Earnings
facts.value: Oct 29, after the close (fiscal Q4 2026)

facts.label: Stock reaction
facts.value: Closed up 2.24% at $105.51 before the print, then down 1.72% after hours

facts.label: Sentiment
facts.value: Moderately bullish on fundamentals, but the stock had already run up

tickers.before: Consensus was EPS of about $0.72 on $9.23B of revenue. Pros watched US comps and whether the turnaround could clear a raised bar, since the stock was up about 13% for the month (Mike Zaccardi's heat map).
tickers.after: Global comps were +7.2% against +6.2% expected, and US comps were +7.7% with transactions up 2.4%. That is the fifth straight quarterly beat. EPS was $0.80 against $0.72. Revenue of $9.14B missed because the China business was sold. International comps were weak at +0.9% against about +3%. Fiscal 2027 guidance: about 4% North America comps, $3.15 to $3.25 EPS, and pricing below CPI. Restaurant analyst Jonathan Maze highlighted that over 80% of North America stores had positive comps, up from 50%.

facts.label: Earnings
facts.value: Oct 29, after the close (call at 3:30 PM CT)

facts.label: Stock reaction
facts.value: Unverified: one retail post claims up over 7% on the day and up 4% after hours. I could not confirm this from a price source

facts.label: Sentiment
facts.value: Mixed: share gains and margins good, Q4 guide soft

tickers.before: The bar was adjusted EPS of about $0.14 on about $2.58B of adjusted revenue. Pros watched market share gains (6.2% of purchases, 14.3% of refinances), mortgage rates at a 3-year high, and synergies from the Redfin and Mr. Cooper deals.
tickers.after: GAAP revenue was $3.28B and adjusted revenue was $2.57B, roughly in line. Adjusted EPS of $0.15 beat by a penny. Adjusted EBITDA of $748M and adjusted net income of $419M were slightly light. The adjusted EBITDA margin of 29% was the highest in about five years. The Q4 adjusted revenue guide of $2.1B to $2.3B implies about a 10% drop, which ties it to rates. Discussion on X was thin and mostly bots and retail. Few institutional voices posted.

tickers.topTheme: AI segment over half of revenue, Tesla merger talk

facts.label: What SPCX is
facts.value: SpaceX Class A stock on Nasdaq. It IPO'd at $135 on June 12, 2026

facts.label: Earnings
facts.value: Oct 20, after the close (Q3 2026, its second report as a public company)

facts.label: Stock reaction
facts.value: Up about 8.6% to about $160 on Oct 21, then fully gave it back. $144.75 on Oct 22, about $138 on Oct 30

facts.label: Sentiment
facts.value: Bullish from the Street, but the tape faded it

facts.label: Street moves
facts.value: JPMorgan raised its target to $500 from $240, Barclays to $300, Wells Fargo to $274, Citi to $240, UBS to $230

tickers.before: Consensus was about $12.7B to $13B of revenue. Pros watched AI compute and Starlink growth and a possible Tesla merger. Gary Black predicted SpaceX would buy Tesla at $420 a share in stock.
tickers.after: Revenue was $14.6B, up 161%. EPS was $0.35 against $0.13. It posted its first profit as a public company, at $4.4B. The AI segment (AI cloud, Grok, Cursor) was about $7.6B, over half of revenue, with an adjusted EBITDA margin of about 66% per call notes. Musk called a Tesla merger a 'good idea', and both boards have special committees. Sell-side targets jumped, but the stock round-tripped within two days. Pros described the fade as valuation and supply concerns rather than a problem with the quarter.
tickers.controversy: Tesla merger talk dominates the reach, which is mostly hype. Treat posts about deal terms as speculation.

method: I searched X with date limits around each earnings date, using cashtags, company names and themes. I also ran searches limited to a list of professional accounts, such as research desks, the sell-side, former fund managers and trade journalists. Posts were ranked by likes, reposts and views. Memes, options-flow promoters, bot recaps and low-follower hype were dropped. X's API cannot filter by engagement, so ranking was done by hand. Stock moves and analyst targets come from CNBC, AP, Yahoo Finance, Benzinga and Investing.com. Engagement counts were captured on Oct 30 and will keep changing. The RKT stock move is unverified. Pro reach on X is modest overall. The best-known names (sell-side analysts, PMs) mostly do not post on X, so the Street views here come from news coverage of their notes.
